title: Skippering a charter yacht: leading the crew
lead: On a bareboat charter the skipper is responsible for the yacht and for everyone on board, often with a crew of friends or family. Good skippering is mostly clear jobs, calm calls, honest decisions and looking after people.
description: How to skipper a bareboat charter yacht: legal responsibility, choosing and briefing the crew, jobs and calls for manoeuvres, planning the day, saying no, chores, seasickness, heat, fatigue, children and the debrief.
summary: The skipper named on the charter papers is responsible in law for the yacht and everyone on board.
Before every manoeuvre, give each person one job, and during it let only one voice give the calls.
Decide early and say no clearly when weather, alcohol or tiredness make a plan unsafe.
Watch your crew for seasickness, heat and fatigue, and debrief each manoeuvre calmly, without blame.
